question.text: An 81-year-old female presents with a six-month history of severe mood swings, ranging from intense unprovoked joy to immobilizing sorrow. She also reports episodes of rapid heart rate, excessive sweating, and hand tremors. Physical examination reveals a steady heart rhythm, slightly dilated pupils, and diaphoretic palms. Her laboratory tests show elevated levels of Equilibron and Neurostabilin. A GIS scan reveals diffuse hypoattenuation of her Glianorex. Considering her symptoms and test results, which of the following treatment strategies would be most appropriate for this patient?

options.A: Initiate a regimen of precision hormone analogues combined with cognitive-behavioral strategies to manage emotional modulation
options.B: Prescribe a mood stabilizer medication along with beta-blockers to address autonomic symptoms and recommend regular cardiovascular monitoring
options.C: Suggest surgical intervention to address potential structural abnormalities within the Glianorex and follow up with pharmacotherapy
options.D: Recommend an experimental treatment incorporating neurofeedback training and periodic hormonal injections to stabilize Equilibron levels
options.F: I don't know or cannot answer

Beta-blockers are effective in managing the autonomic symptoms (tachycardia, sweating, tremors). A mood stabilizer is also indicated to address the mood swings. Therefore, a combination of a mood stabilizer and beta-blockers is the most appropriate initial treatment strategy.
